## 1. Purpose, scope and roles

Enable leadership to evaluate the scoped system, make resourced decisions and verify follow-through. A meeting held or minutes signed is not proof that the system is healthy.

Process identity: **P20**. Accountable process owner: **Management review chair**.
The roles in the table perform the work. Actual appointments and deputies must be
recorded before adoption; fictional names in the example are not appointments.
This is an administrative IMS workflow, not permission to operate, isolate, repair
or restart chemical equipment.

## 2. Trigger and prerequisites

**Trigger:** Configured management-review schedule, major change, significant failed control or escalation beyond delegated authority.

**Required inputs/resources:** Agreed scope, competent decision-makers and authority/quorum rules, prior actions, performance/risk/assurance evidence and an agenda. Configure required inputs against the actual adopted standards and obligations; the starter agenda is not a complete ISO checklist.

## 3. Process map and controlled steps

Request inputs → validate evidence → circulate agenda → discuss and decide → communicate actions → verify implementation/outcome → carry forward or reopen

Use the [worksheet](ORR-FRM-MRV-001_REVIEW-THE-SYSTEM-AND-TRACK-DECISIONS-WORKSHEET.md). Each row below is a discrete proposed control:
who and when are explicit; the action/method and acceptance test are in the step;
where is the scoped process and its authorized private record store; why is the
purpose above, refined to the linked objective/risk in each execution record.
Copy each adopted control into the risk/control register with its own stable ID.

| Step | Performer | Trigger/frequency | Action and method/criteria | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Review coordinator | Before the scheduled meeting | Request scoped inputs with owners and cut-off dates: prior decisions; context/obligations; customer/worker feedback; objectives; process/output performance; environmental/OH&S information; resources/providers; risks; audits/incidents/corrective actions; change; continuity readiness; improvement. Mark missing or stale evidence. | Agenda/input register and evidence references with dates/confidence. |
| 2 | Chair | Before and at meeting | Check authority, participants and missing material inputs. Hear relevant worker/process-owner views. Hold unsupported conclusions; arrange competent advice or an extraordinary review where urgency requires. | Attendance/authority record, gaps and escalation decisions. |
| 3 | Authorized management participants | For each agenda decision | Record issue, evidence, options, decision/rationale, dissent, resources, owner, due date, limits and acceptance criteria. Link parent risk/objective/control; risk acceptance follows delegated limits. | Attributable decision IDs and action records. |
| 4 | Coordinator and action owners | After meeting and at agreed checkpoints | Confirm recipients understand assigned decisions. Monitor dates, dependencies and implementation evidence; escalate overdue items to the chair with impact, not merely a red status. | Acknowledgments, action updates and escalations. |
| 5 | Outcome reviewer and chair | At specified verification trigger and subsequent review | Test whether the agreed result occurred. Close an action only after required implementation and outcome evidence; reopen failed results while retaining prior closure history. Carry unresolved issues to the next agenda. | Outcome result, closure/reopening decision and next agenda reference. |

## 4. Acceptance, holds and escalation

Every substantive decision has an authorized decision-maker, evidence, resource disposition, owner, deadline and verification criteria. Open issues survive into the next review; conclusions state exact scope and limitations.

Where evidence is absent or competence/authority insufficient, record a specific held decision, interim arrangements, owner and due date. Do not record “system effective” from attendance or a partial review. An action overdue or ineffective remains visible until legitimately resolved.

Measure overdue decisions/actions, missing mandatory evidence and failed control
executions in this process; define population and review interval locally. Do not
interpret “no reports” as “no problems.” Review both performance and reporting access.

## 5. Outputs, interfaces and records

Send scope/context decisions to risk owners; risk decisions to objective/control
owners; changed methods/forms to document control; performance and unresolved
issues to management review. The receiving owner acknowledges the handoff.
Record the incoming ID, outgoing ID, sender, receiver and acceptance or rejection.
Use one authoritative operational index for completed worksheets and evidence;
retain original event identity and template revision. The public examples are not
that operational index. The worksheet defines fields and filing rules.

## 6. Configure and test before use

Replace organizational placeholders; confirm scope, actual roles, lawful obligations,
approval limits, response times, retention/access and dependencies. Have relevant
specialists verify technical criteria. Execute one normal case and one held or
failed case with intended users; record findings before approval. Use
[the shared acceptance protocol](ORR-ASP-IMP-001_BEGINNER-KIT-ACCEPTANCE.md).

## Sources, tailoring and history

Original ORR learning design, based on the user-requested ORCA chain and practical
implementation needs. A purchased commercial pack was reviewed privately for
coverage and usability lessons before drafting; this is not a clean-room claim.
No vendor procedure, diagram, spreadsheet, clause text or completed record is
included. Source provenance and limits are recorded in ORR-REG-REL-002. Existing
ORCA attribution remains in the repository SOURCES.md. These are proposed internal
methods, not verified interpretations of ISO requirements or a certification checklist.

Adopters may change layout, terminology, software and proportional detail. Keep
traceable identity, accountable decisions, applicable obligations, evidence,
failure routes and approval boundaries. Unknown is not not-applicable. A mandatory
departure requires a recorded decision within legitimate authority; internal
acceptance cannot waive external duties. Use the linked document-control procedure.
